rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: Assumption: a track's artist is reached via Track → Album → Artist, and I count distinct GenreIds per artist.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.Name
ORDER BY SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) DESC
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is computed from InvoiceLine as UnitPrice × Quantity, grouped by track genre, with tracks lacking a genre labeled as their NULL group.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
  SELECT i2.CustomerId
  FROM Invoice i2
  JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
  WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
);
rows.note: Assumption: a customer "bought" a track if it appears in an InvoiceLine linked to one of their invoices, and genres are matched by Genre.Name.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS Month, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY Month ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2011, grouped by calendar month.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
) AS f
WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01';
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and we count customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.
I'm assuming invoice revenue is the sum of `Total` per calendar year, based on `InvoiceDate`.

rows.sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT p.PlaylistId, p.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS artist_count
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT Name, artist_count FROM c
WHERE artist_count = (SELECT MAX(artist_count) FROM c);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) sub
rows.note: Assuming "contain tracks from more than one genre" means an invoice has InvoiceLines whose tracks span at least two distinct GenreIds.

rows.sql:
WITH rep_rev AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS RepName, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice i
  JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
  JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
  WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, RepName
)
SELECT RepName, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM rep_rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rep_rev);
rows.note: I'm assuming "revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` for invoices dated in 2010, attributed to each customer's support rep.

rows.sql:
WITH yg AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS Year, g.Name AS Genre,
         SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Invoice i ON i.InvoiceId = il.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
  GROUP BY Year, Genre
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT Year, Genre, Revenue,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Year ORDER BY Revenue DESC) AS rnk
  FROM yg
)
SELECT Year, Genre, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 2
ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity from InvoiceLine, the year comes from InvoiceDate, and ties at second place are all returned.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CustomerId,
         SUM(CASE WHEN substr(InvoiceDate,1,4) = '2013' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS total_2013,
         SUM(CASE WHEN substr(InvoiceDate,1,4) = '2012' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS total_2012
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_spent_more_in_2013
FROM yearly
WHERE total_2013 > total_2012;
rows.note: I'll compare each customer's total invoice amount in 2013 against 2012, treating a customer with no invoices in a year as having spent 0 that year.

rows.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT Total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Total) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM Invoice
)
SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total
FROM ordered
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2);
rows.note: Assuming "median" means the middle value of Invoice.Total across all invoices (averaging the two middle values if the count is even).

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
  FROM PlaylistTrack pt
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  JOIN Artist ar ON ar.ArtistId = al.ArtistId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
)
SELECT Name, PlaylistCount
FROM counts
WHERE PlaylistCount = (SELECT MAX(PlaylistCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assumption: "tracks appear in playlists" means counting distinct playlists containing at least one track by the artist (via Track → Album → Artist), and I'll return all tied top artists.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY od.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 5;
rows.note: Assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from "Order Details", summed per product and joined to Products for the name.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM Products p JOIN Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName;
rows.note: I'm treating "most expensive" as the highest `Products.UnitPrice` within each category, keeping all tied products and including discontinued ones.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.CustomerID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021'
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CompanyName, r.revenue
FROM rev r
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = r.CustomerID
WHERE r.revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note: I'll calculate revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), summed per customer over orders dated in 2021, and return the top customer (all ties).

rows.sql: SELECT month, order_count FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month) WHERE order_count = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER)));
rows.note: Assuming OrderDate is stored as text in a standard date format, I'll count 2021 orders by calendar month and return all months tied for the top count.
The database has no orders from 1997. The Orders table's OrderDate values range from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, so no employee can be credited with orders in that year.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assuming "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the difference in days between OrderDate and ShippedDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct_of_2023_revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, filtered to orders dated in 2023, and that the share is taken over all 2023 revenue.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12);
rows.note: I'm assuming "every month of 2020" means each of the 12 calendar months has at least one order dated in 2020.

rows.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_totals
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg);
rows.note: I'm treating each order's value as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its lines, and averaging those values per employee.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT s.CompanyName AS SupplierName,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
  JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
  GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName
)
SELECT SupplierName, Revenue
FROM rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note: Assuming revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, grouped by supplier, for orders dated in 2018.

rows.sql:
WITH y AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units2022
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
),
d AS (
  SELECT y.ProductID, y.units2021, y.units2022, (y.units2022 - y.units2021) AS increase
  FROM y
)
SELECT p.ProductName, d.units2021, d.units2022, d.increase
FROM d
JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
WHERE d.increase = (SELECT MAX(increase) FROM d);
rows.note: I'm assuming "units sold" means the sum of `Quantity` in Order Details, grouped by the year of `OrderDate`, and that the increase is 2022 minus 2021.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(o.ShippedDate) > julianday(o.RequiredDate) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS LatePercentage
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "arrived after the required date" means ShippedDate is later than RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT year, order_count, SUM(order_count) OVER (ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_order_count FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS year, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders GROUP BY year) ORDER BY year
rows.note: Assuming "year" means the calendar year of OrderDate, I'll count orders per year and accumulate them in year order.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID,
         strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) AS yr,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) IN ('2018', '2019')
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID, yr
),
growth AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2018' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS rev_2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2019' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS rev_2019,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2019' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2018' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS growth
  FROM rev
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS employee,
       g.rev_2018, g.rev_2019, g.growth
FROM growth g
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = g.EmployeeID
WHERE g.growth = (SELECT MAX(growth) FROM growth)
rows.note: Assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), grouped by the year of OrderDate, and growth = 2019 minus 2018.
